Question_text: Y2M is a bus operating company in the public sector. One of its objectives is to break even on every bus route. Most of its competitors are in the private sector. Y2M wants to increase the number of customers using its buses. The Finance Director has been looking at some cost data shown in Table1. This is because Y2M plans to review its pricing methods. She is worried other businesses pay workers a higher wage rate and some of its drivers may leave. She said: 'To pay the same wage rate would increase variable cost to $2.20 per passenger per journey.'
image: A table titled 'Table 1: Cost and price data for one Y2M route' with two columns. The first column lists categories: 'Number of passengers per day', 'Price per passenger per journey', 'Fixed costs per week', 'Variable cost per passenger per journey'. The second column provides corresponding data: '90', '$2.50', '$300', '$2'.
Sub_topic: Differences: private vs public sector objectives
Different objectives: survival, growth, profit, market share
Classify private sector, public sector in mixed economy
Concept of break-even
Pricing methods: cost plus, competitive, penetration, skimming, promotional
Financial rewards: wage, salary, bonus, commission, profit sharing

Parts.part_text: What is meant by ‘break-even'?
Calculate the revenue per day.
Identify and explain two objectives Y2M might have if it was in the private sector.
Identify and explain two pricing methods Y2M could use.
Do you think Y2M should pay its workers the same wage rate as its competitors? Justify your answer.

Question_text: Kate is an entrepreneur. Two years ago she left her job as a fashion designer at a multinational company. She started up BBB, a women's sportswear clothing business. BBB targets a market segment of high income consumers. BBB's products are sold in 3 retail shops and also through its website. Kate said: 'I saw a gap in the market and took the risk. Obtaining the finance I needed from the bank was not easy. I enjoy making decisions such as using leaflets to promote the clothes.' BBB's revenue target for next year is $500 000.
Sub_topic: Characteristics of successful entrepreneurs
Reasons for finance: start-up, expansion, working capital
Greater risk for new businesses
How/why segment: age, socio-economic, location, gender
Benefits of segmentation
Forms: advertising, sales promotion, influence on sales

Parts.part_text: What is meant by 'entrepreneur'?
Identify two reasons why obtaining finance may not be easy for a new business.
Identify and explain two possible reasons why Kate decided to start up her own business.
Identify and explain two reasons why segmenting the market might help BBB.
Do you think that using leaflets is the best way for Kate to promote her products? Justify your answer.

Question_text: BVC makes a range of paints. It exports 60% of its products. The Managing Director has been looking at BVC's cash-flow forecast shown in Table 2. He said: 'Success is not just about our return on capital employed.' The Managing Director is worried about the introduction of new legal controls to protect the environment. This will mean BVC will have to reduce the number of chemicals that are used to make paint. He thinks these new legal controls will be bad for business.
image: A table titled 'Table 2: Extract of cash flow forecast for the period July-September 2019 ($000)'. It has columns for 'July', 'August', and 'September', and rows for 'Cash inflow' (600, 560, 620), 'Cash outflow' (560, 540, 580), 'Net cash flow' (40, 20, Y), 'Opening balance' (X, 60, 80), and 'Closing balance' (60, 80, 120).
Sub_topic: What is cash-flow forecast, construction, importance
Amend, complete forecast
Interpret forecast
Ratios: gross profit margin, profit margin, return on capital employed, current ratio, acid test ratio
Impact on importers, exporters: prices, competitiveness, profitability
Legal controls: pollution
Business impact on environment: global warming

Parts.part_text: What is meant by 'return on capital employed'?
Calculate the following values: X: Y:
Identify and explain two reasons why a cash flow forecast might be important for BVC.
Identify and explain two possible problems for BVC when exporting its products.
The Managing Director thinks the new legal controls to protect the environment will be bad for business. Do you agree? Justify your answer.

Question_text: FGH is a private limited company. FGH has a tall hierarchical organisational structure. It is a book retailer which plans to take over one of its competitors for $800m. If the takeover happens, FGH would have 6500 bookshops across 20 countries. FGH's Managing Director said: 'We expect to reduce total costs by $300m each year after the takeover. We will stop all off-the-job training of employees.' The Managing Director thinks FGH would benefit from becoming a public limited company but some of the other directors cannot decide if this is a good idea.
Sub_topic: Features: sole traders, partnerships, private/public limited companies, franchises, joint ventures
Hierarchical structures: levels, span of control, chain of command, chain of tall/short
Ways to grow: internal/external
Benefits, limitations: induction, on-the-job, off-the-job training
Classify costs: fixed, variable, average, total

Parts.part_text: What is meant by 'off-the-job training'?
What is meant by 'total cost'?
Identify and explain two advantages of FGH having a tall hierarchical organisational structure.
Identify and explain one advantage and one disadvantage to FGH of becoming a public limited company.
Do you think FGH should take over the other business? Justify your answer.
